title: Protocol to isolate and analyze mouse bone marrow derived dendritic cells (BMDC)
protocol: Euthanize the mice with inhaled anesthetics followed by cervical dislocation.
Sterilize the hind legs and back by spraying with 70% ethanol.
Pin the paws to a suitable surface.
Cut the midline of the back and continue cutting to expose the femurs.
Place the mouse face down on the dissecting platform.
Cut the skin at the back and expose the legs.
Cut the femur at the hip joint, then take out the whole leg.
Separate the femur by cutting the knee joint.
Separate the tibia from the paw.
Cut off the epiphyses on both sides of the bone.
Carefully insert a syringe filled with DC medium into the bone and flush out bone marrow into a 50 mL falcon tube.
Unpin the right leg and peel the skin off toward the midline.
Cut the adductor muscles toward the midline and sever the leg between the hip joint and the spine.
Once the leg is detached from the body, separate the femur from the tibia by cutting the knee joint.
Cut away the paw and remove excess tissue from the bone using paper towels and gently rubbing off the tissue.
Cut the paw off distal to the ankle, and peel off the remaining skin.
Hold the distal end of the tibia with a forceps so that the knee joint is pointing away from you and the leg is vertical.
Spray both legs with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol.
Collect femurs and tibiae working on a 70% (vol/vol) ethanol–soaked towel.
Strip the calf tissue by pushing it down toward the knee using slightly opened scissors.
Grip the tibia and femur with two sets of forceps and gently push against the direction of the knee joint until the tibia breaks right at the knee.
Remove any hanging tissue from the tibia and place it on a towel.
Recover the femur in the same way, snapping off the knee.
Hold the fleshy end of each bone piece in a dry paper towel and pull the bone with forceps to remove remaining flesh.
Squeeze and rub the remaining fleshy part in the towel to clean the bone further.
Collect the cleaned bones in a small Petri dish filled with medium on ice.
Disinfect the bones by soaking them in 70% (vol/vol) ethanol for 1 min in the first well of a prepared 6-well plate.
Place the bones in a second well containing 2 mL BMDC culture medium.
Move the bones to a third well filled with 2 mL BMDC medium.
Collect 10 mL of fresh BMDC culture medium in a 10-mL syringe.
Attach a 27-gauge needle to the syringe.
Remove the tibia from the Petri dish and cut it off at the ankle joint at an angle.
Hold the tibia over a fresh 50-mL tube, with the narrow end pointing down.
Gently squirt medium onto the tibia using the needle.
Insert the needle gently at the top end of the marrow and squirt medium.
Pull back the needle and insert it again.
Squirt with brief, high pressure pushes to flush the bone marrow.
Push the needle in further until the epiphysis has been crossed and medium comes out at the bottom end of the bone.
Continue flushing a couple more times until the bone is white; then discard the bone.
Repeat steps for the femur by cutting off at the hip joint as with the tibia.
Use the same 50-mL tube to collect marrow from the femur.
Add an additional 20 mL of BMDC culture medium to the 50-mL tube using a glass pipet.
Gently suspend the marrow in the BMDC medium with the pipet.
Pass the cell suspension through a 70-μm cell strainer into a new 50-mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 250 × g at 22°–23°C for 5 min to pellet the cells.
Discard the supernatant carefully by aspirating it.
Add 5 mL of ice-cold lysis buffer for RBC lysis per Falcon tube and gently tap the tube to mix.
Incubate the tubes on ice for 5 min after mixing.
Add 10 mL of RPMI medium to dilute the buffer following RBC lysis.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 250 × g at 22°–23°C for 5 min to pellet cells.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 18 mL of culture medium and mix well.
Seed bone marrow cells from one mouse into a 6-well plate using 3 mL per well with 10-25 ng/mL GM-CSF.
Incubate the cell cultures at 37°C and humidified 5% CO2 for initial seeding.
Gently wash cells with pre-warmed PBS on day 2, 4, and 6.
Supply cells with 3 mL of new pre-warmed DC-medium containing freshly added 20 ng/mL GM-CSF.
Add 10 μg/mL acetylated low density lipoprotein (acLDL) or control to create an atherosclerotic environment on day 6.
Pre-warm the DC-medium at 37°C in the water bath (GM-CSF does not have to be added).
Collect the dendritic cells as described in the following steps 25–28.
Be careful to avoid collecting the highly adherent cells by not pipetting too forcefully.
Discard highly adherent cells and enrich or sort for CD11c+ cells.
Remove the medium by aspirating.
Collect the cells.
Pour 2 mL fresh medium over the cells in one well of the 6 well plate with a glass pipette.
Pipet up and pour over again, repeat this 2 times.
Transfer the medium containing the DCs into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Repeat this with all wells of the 6 well plate.
Pool the cells of one plate in one 50 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 250 × g at 22°–23°C for 5 min to pellet the cells.
Discard the supernatant.
